A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same algorithms and theoretical contributions. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; v2 adds Appendix H.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 2 report original simulation results for Algorithms 2 and 3 under KL and chi-squared uncertainty sets.

after.justification: v2 retains those simulations and adds original baseline comparisons and larger-MDP experiments in Appendix H.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same empirical transition estimates, Bellman equations, discount calibration, anchoring procedure, and outputs. The added proof sketch and experiments introduce no method component.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from the two-state Hard MDP family, whose actions induce identical transitions, to randomly generated 20-state, 30-action instances. Appendix H materially broadens the represented transition structures and includes stronger perturbations outside the theoretical uncertainty-radius condition.

E2.justification: Appendix H adds one external comparator, DR RVI Q-learning from Wang et al. (2023e), evaluated against both proposed algorithms in Table 2 and Figure 3. v1 cites this work but does not evaluate it.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces comparisons at nine sample budgets from 10 to 100000, with delta = 0.1 for the baseline comparison and delta = 0.4 for larger MDPs. Algorithms 2 and 3 use distinct larger instances. The existing Section 5 protocol is retained.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a robustness check at delta = 0.4, explicitly violating Assumption 2, and examines whether convergence remains near n^(-1/2). This extends the analysis beyond the original convergence demonstrations, without adding component ablations or a systematic sensitivity sweep.

E5.justification: Section 5 retains its single independent estimate per plotted point and regression analysis. Appendix H introduces no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New results establish baseline comparisons and larger-instance convergence. At 100000 samples, Table 2 reports errors of 0.0261 for DR RVI Q-learning, 0.00117 for Reduction to DMDP, and 0.00123 for Anchored DR-AMDP. Table 3 adds results on distinct larger instances, which do not support a direct ranking between the algorithms. Original Figure 2 results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorems, and proofs in Appendices A–G are unchanged. The new Section 4.2 proof sketch summarizes existing derivations, including the Bellman-operator error bounds. Definition 3.3 is reworded equivalently for the finite policy class.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: two algorithms, finite-sample guarantees under uniform ergodicity and sufficiently small uncertainty sets, and operation without prior mixing-time knowledge. The added literature-review sentence reiterates existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly interprets the larger-MDP results as demonstrating effectiveness despite violating Assumption 2, and calls them validation of the theoretical guarantees. This extends the applicability discussion, although such experiments cannot validate guarantees outside their assumptions. Existing conclusion limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H supplies technical details for the added experiments: MDP dimensions, uncertainty radii, and normally distributed transition draws with a Uniform[0,100] scale followed by normalization. These are new disclosures, although handling of negative draws and baseline tuning remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The bibliography and theoretical novelty positioning are unchanged. Appendix H adds an explicit empirical superiority claim over the already cited DR RVI Q-learning method, extending the paper's positioning relative to Wang et al. (2023e).

P1.justification: v2 adds a proof roadmap, Appendix H, acknowledgments, author-footnote updates, and localized clarifications while retaining the main narrative and section order. Appendix H contains near-duplicated paragraphs describing the larger-MDP experiments.

P2.justification: Appendix H adds Tables 2–3, Figure 3, and two final-page convergence plots. Existing Figures 1–2 are relocated without changing their content, and Table 1 gains a definition cross-reference. The overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: The proof roadmap improves accessibility, while the first external baseline comparison and tests beyond the two-state family modestly strengthen empirical support. These gains are limited by Appendix H's inconsistent p_min = 0.9 description, incomplete transition-generation details, and overstated interpretation of experiments violating Assumption 2. The central algorithms and theoretical guarantees remain unchanged.
